user_reviews.Name: Eric Chan
user_reviews.Description:
Pot Kettle Black is one of those places I’m generally happy to return to. The space is open, warm, and inviting, and it feels like a nice spot to slow down a bit, especially for brunch or a catch-up.

It does get pretty crowded on weekends, so expect a bit of noise and waiting around. Front-of-house service was prompt and friendly when we arrived, which helped, though the kitchen was noticeably slower. Food took a while to come out, but nothing outrageous, just something to be aware of if you’re in a rush.

Food itself was pretty decent across the board. Nothing overcomplicated, just well-executed brunch dishes that do what they’re meant to. The real standout for me was the coffee. Easily one of the better cups in Manchester. Balanced, well made, and clearly something they take seriously here. That alone makes the place worth coming back to.

Prices felt fair for the location and quality, especially given how central Barton Arcade is. You don’t feel like you’re being overcharged just for sitting somewhere trendy, which I appreciate.

Overall, it’s a nice, dependable place to meet friends, chat, and enjoy a good coffee. Go when you’re not in a rush, expect it to be busy on weekends, and you’ll likely leave feeling satisfied rather than stressed.

user_reviews.Name: Ramsha Bukhari
user_reviews.Description:
I left PKB feeling genuinely humiliated and unwelcome.

I visited at around 11am to get some work done and, as a paying customer, ordered food and a drink. I politely asked if I could move to a slightly bigger table so I had more space to work, but I was refused and told that the restaurant was “busy.”

What made the situation particularly uncomfortable was what happened next. Two men left one of the larger tables, so I moved over to it. The manager on duty — the woman with curly hair — then made me get up from the table, telling me that the men would be coming back.

They did not return while I was there. Instead, that same table was later given to another party.

There were also several other larger tables visibly unoccupied at the time, as shown in the photos I took during my visit and have attached to this review. I completely understand that restaurants need to manage their seating, but the way this was handled simply did not make sense to me and left me feeling singled out.

After I had finished and paid my bill, I calmly told the manager that the experience had made me feel discriminated against. There was no apology, no concern and no attempt to understand why I felt that way. Instead, she told me, “It’s fine, you can leave a bad review,” and then walked away.

That response was what made the experience even more upsetting. If a customer tells a manager that they feel they have been discriminated against, I would expect the concern to at least be taken seriously rather than dismissed.

I have lived in the UK for quite some time and have always found Manchester to be an incredibly diverse and welcoming city. This was the first time here that I left an establishment genuinely questioning whether I had been treated differently because of my background.

I won’t be returning, and I will be sharing my experience with others because I would never want anyone else to leave feeling the way I did.

You go to a café to spend your time, order food and drinks, pay for the experience and expect to be treated with basic courtesy and respect. You certainly don’t pay to leave feeling humiliated or singled out.

I’ve attached photos from around the time of my visit so people can see the circumstances for themselves and make their own judgement.

user_reviews.Name: Ace
user_reviews.Description:
I had the absolute pleasure of spending time in the Aspire Lounge at Manchester Airport Terminal 3 recently, and I can honestly say it completely transformed the whole airport experience.

From the moment I walked in, I was welcomed by friendly and professional staff who made the check-in process quick and effortless. The atmosphere inside the lounge is calm, modern, and well-maintained, offering a perfect escape from the busy terminal outside. It’s exactly what you want before a flight—comfortable, quiet, and relaxing.

The seating options were excellent, with plenty of space whether you want to unwind on your own, catch up on work, or sit together as a group. I particularly appreciated the cleanliness throughout the lounge; everything from the tables to the seating areas was spotless and clearly well looked after.

The food and drink selection was another highlight. There was a good variety of hot and cold options, all fresh and regularly replenished. The self-service bar was well stocked, offering a nice range of alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks, and the coffee machine was a lifesaver. It’s great being able to help yourself without long queues or waiting around.

One thing that really stood out to me was the overall ambience. It felt far more premium than expected, with soft lighting, a relaxed vibe, and just the right level of background noise. It made it easy to sit back, recharge, and genuinely enjoy the time before boarding.

Overall, the Aspire Lounge in Terminal 3 is fantastic value for money and a must if you want to start your journey stress-free. I’ll definitely be booking again for future trips—highly recommended!

I’m writing this review while still waiting to get into the Aspire Lounge at Manchester Airport Terminal 2.

I joined the queue almost two hours ago, and after waiting all this time, it is still showing another 10 minutes.

I’ve had DragonPass for years and use it when travelling. At international airports, I normally get lounge access without much trouble. Manchester Terminal 2 has been a completely different experience.

For the last two years, I have not managed to get into Aspire or Escape at T2 using DragonPass. The only times I’ve been able to use these lounges have been when travelling Business Class and getting access through my ticket.

Today I’m travelling with a budget airline because its flight time suited my journey. This is exactly when a paid DragonPass membership should be useful. Instead, I’ve spent almost two hours in a queue and I’m still waiting.

I have used Aspire here before through Business Class access. The lounge is smaller than Escape, and the food selection is fine. The bigger issue is getting through the door in the first place.

If DragonPass members regularly face waits like this at Manchester T2, it is difficult to see what I am paying for. After years of membership, this is the airport where my DragonPass repeatedly fails to provide any practical benefit.

Nearly two hours waiting today, and the clock is still running.

user_reviews.Name: Micky Watts
user_reviews.Description:
Wow. Honestly, Burger King, I would highly recommend that some regional management conduct an audit of the customer service staff working here. Absolutely disgusting behaviour. I think you would agree if you went there.

Firstly, my brother and I walked in and tried to use the electronic kiosk to order food. However, we noticed that only a takeaway option was available. Now my brother insisted that we sit in, so I said, "Well, we can ask the staff." He did this and was met with laughter from the staff. They said "yes" but rolled their eyes at the audacity of us wanting to sit in. God knows why my brother wanted to sit in, by the way, as the tables were messy and they couldn't even empty a bin between them. They were clearly rushed off their feet with the 4 customers in the place. In fact, including the 1 man on security, there were actually more staff members there than customers.

Now my brother is autistic, so he just thought they were friendly...THEY WEREN'T. Anyway, my brother took a while to decide what to get, and again I could see staff members laughing and again rolling their eyes at his choices. He wanted a milkshake, and it felt like he was asking them for a favour. Anyway, once they were done laughing at my brother, I decided I wanted to order a meal as well. Now it was my turn for some eye rolls.

Anyway, once I got my food, I joined my brother at the dirty table, as I said before, though they were clearly busy. It's at this point where I would like to apologise for interrupting STAFF MOVIE NIGHT, as there were 4 members of staff watching something on a phone. If I had known this, I would never have gone to Burger King and ruined their plans. Anyway, I felt bad about this, so I decided to clear the rubbish from our table and tried to put it in the overflowing bin.

In my time spent there (20 mins), I believe I did more work there than most of the staff on shift, just by clearing my table. Ultimately, I would highly recommend that management review these individuals, as I am confused about what they are being paid for. After seeing the recent reviews, I am also aware that I'm not the only person here with this opinion about customer service skills.

The only positive was that the food was fine, not bad, but not amazing, shame the same can't be said for the customer service and floor staff.

user_reviews.Name: Jason Dugdale
user_reviews.Description:
Been meaning to try this place for a long time now and finally did.  I had the Delhi Spice special kebab and in terms of value, it’s outstanding. For under £8 you get doner, chicken tikka and a seek kebab all stir fried in their tomato tandoori sauce with onions placed on a fresh naan bread cooked in a tandoori clay oven.  Whilst the stir fry sauce is not overpowering, it disguises some of the individual flavours of the meat and I would best describe it as a sort of shashlik kebab. In terms of portion size, it’s very generous and comes with 2 tubs containing yoghurt mint sauce and a mild chilli sauce.  In terms of price, for the size of the kebab and the time taken to cook it in the sauce, the value is outstanding and it’s definitely a bargain.

The takeaway does a range of kebabs that are mostly stir fried but you can also have them not stir fried.  I don’t think this will be a regular takeaway for me but I shall certainly return in the future!
